segments.arabic: [209] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن هشام عن أبيه عن عائشة أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Hisham, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: إذا نعس أحدكم وهو يصلي فليرقد حتى يذهب عنه النوم فإن أحدكم إذا صلى وهو ناعس لا يدري لعله يستغفر فيسب نفسه
segments.english: “When one of you becomes drowsy while praying, let him lie down until the sleepiness leaves him. For if one of you prays while drowsy, he does not know: he may seek forgiveness but revile himself.”

notes: The full chain, drowsiness, lying down and contrast between seeking forgiveness and reviling oneself remain. No legal explanation or condition is added to the narration.

segments.arabic: [210] حدثنا أبو معمر قال: حدثنا عبد الوارث حدثنا أيوب عن أبي قلابة عن أنس عن النبي ﷺ قال:
segments.english: Abu Ma‘mar related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Warith related to us. Ayyub related to us, from Abu Qilabah, from Anas, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

segments.arabic: إذا نعس أحدكم في الصلاة فلينم حتى يعلم ما يقرأ
segments.english: “When one of you becomes drowsy during prayer, let him sleep until he knows what he is reciting.”

notes: Both consecutive reporting verbs are retained. The final source verb is reciting, without replacing it with a general saying or adding a separate explanation.

segments.arabic: [211] حدثنا محمد بن يوسف قال: حدثنا سفيان عن عمرو بن عامر قال: سمعت أنسا
segments.english: Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from ‘Amr ibn ‘Amir, who said: I heard Anas.

segments.arabic: ح قال وحدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا يحيى عن سفيان قال: حدثني عمرو بن عامر عن أنس قال:
segments.english: Another chain: He said: And Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from Sufyan, who said: ‘Amr ibn ‘Amir related to me, from Anas, who said:

segments.arabic: كان النبي ﷺ يتوضأ عند كل صلاة قلت: كيف كنتم تصنعون قال يجزي أحدنا الوضوء ما لم يحدث
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to perform ablution at every prayer. I asked: “What did you use to do?” He said: “Ablution would suffice for each of us as long as he did not break it.”

notes: Both chains and the ح transfer marker remain in order. Another chain renders the notation, as in earlier prototype entries; no first-chain body is invented. The follow-up question and answer remain in the report.

segments.arabic: [212] حدثنا خالد بن مخلد قال: حدثنا سليمان قال: حدثني يحيى بن سعيد قال: أخبرني بشير بن يسار قال: أخبرني سويد بن النعمان قال
segments.english: Khalid ibn Makhlad related to us. He said: Sulayman related to us. He said: Yahya ibn Sa‘id related to me. He said: Bashir ibn Yasar informed me. He said: Suwayd ibn al-Nu‘man informed me. He said:

segments.arabic: خرجنا مع رسول الله ﷺ عام خيبر حتى إذا كنا بالصهباء صلى لنا رسول الله ﷺ العصر فلما صلى دعا بالأطعمة فلم يؤت إلا بالسويق فأكلنا وشربنا ثم قام النبي ﷺ إلى المغرب فمضمض ثم صلى لنا المغرب ولم يتوضأ
segments.english: We went out with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the year of Khaybar. When we were at al-Sahba’, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, led us in the ‘Asr prayer. When he had prayed, he called for food, but only sawiq was brought. We ate and drank. Then the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, rose for Maghrib, rinsed his mouth, and led us in the Maghrib prayer without performing ablution.

notes: The full chain and every prayer transition remain. This form says we ate and drank; no water ingredient, conquest detail or moistening action from other accounts is inserted. Sawiq remains the source food name.

segments.arabic: [213] حدثنا عثمان قال: حدثنا جرير عن منصور عن مجاهد عن ابن عباس قال
segments.english: ‘Uthman related to us. He said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said:

segments.arabic: مر النبي ﷺ بحائط من حيطان المدينة أو مكة فسمع صوت إنسانين يعذبان في قبورهما، فقال النبي ﷺ يعذبان وما يعذبان في كبير، ثم قال بلى كان أحدهما لا يستتر من بوله وكان الآخر يمشي بالنميمة ثم دعا بجريدة فكسرها كسرتين فوضع على كل قبر منهما كسرة فقيل له يا رسول الله لم فعلت هذا قال لعله أن يخفف عنهما ما لم تيبسا أو إلى أن ييبسا
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, passed by a garden among the gardens of Madinah or Makkah. He heard the voices of two people being punished in their graves. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “They are being punished, but they are not being punished for something great.” Then he said: “Yes. One of them did not guard himself from his urine, and the other used to go about carrying tales.” Then he called for a palm stalk, broke it into two pieces, and placed a piece on each of their graves. He was asked: “Messenger of Allah, why did you do this?” He said: “Perhaps their punishment will be lightened as long as the two do not dry out—or until they dry out.”

notes: The selected Madinah-or-Makkah order remains; the historical print reverses the cities. Both final drying-time alternatives remain. The selected palm stalk has no added fresh/green adjective here.

The apparent contrast between not something great and Yes remains without inserting the comparisons’ explanatory parentheticals about ease of avoidance or seriousness. Namimah is rendered carrying tales, rather than conflating it with backbiting. The chapter title remains outside the narration.

segments.arabic: [214] حدثنا يعقوب بن إبراهيم قال: حدثنا إسماعيل بن إبراهيم قال: حدثني روح بن القاسم قال: حدثني عطاء بن أبي ميمونة عن أنس بن مالك قال:
segments.english: Ya‘qub ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Isma‘il ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Rawh ibn al-Qasim related to me. He said: ‘Ata’ ibn Abi Maymunah related to me, from Anas ibn Malik, who said:

segments.arabic: كان النبي ﷺ إذا تبرز لحاجته أتيته بماء فيغسل به
segments.english: When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out to relieve himself, I would bring him water with which he would wash himself.

notes: The selected Prophet designation remains; the historical print says Messenger of Allah. The source’s washing action is kept without inserting a named body part from the English EPUB. The chapter introduction remains separately preserved in Arabic.

segments.arabic: [215] حدثنا محمد بن المثنى قال: حدثنا محمد بن خازم قال: حدثنا الأعمش عن مجاهد عن طاوس عن ابن عباس قال
segments.english: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Khazim related to us. He said: Al-A‘mash related to us, from Mujahid, from Tawus, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said:

segments.arabic: مر النبي ﷺ بقبرين، فقال إنهما ليعذبان وما يعذبان في كبير أما أحدهما فكان لا يستتر من البول وأما الآخر فكان يمشي بالنميمة ثم أخذ جريدة رطبة فشقها نصفين فغرز في كل قبر واحدة قالوا يا رسول الله لم فعلت هذا قال لعله يخفف عنهما ما لم ييبسا
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, passed by two graves and said: “They are being punished, but they are not being punished for something great. One of them did not guard himself from urine, and the other used to go about carrying tales.” Then he took a fresh palm stalk, split it into two halves, and planted one in each grave. They asked: “Messenger of Allah, why did you do this?” He said: “Perhaps their punishment will be lightened as long as the two do not dry out.”

segments.arabic: قال ابن المثنى وحدثنا وكيع قال: حدثنا الأعمش قال: سمعت مجاهدا مثله يستتر من بوله
segments.english: Ibn al-Muthanna said: And Waki‘ related to us. He said: Al-A‘mash related to us. He said: I heard Mujahid relate the same: “guard himself from his urine.”

notes: The complete closing Ibn al-Muthanna–Waki‘–al-A‘mash transmission and its selected wording fragment remain. Both inspected prints end this closing note after something similar; the digital source adds يستتر من بوله, reflected as a quoted wording fragment, without silently adding a repeated negative verb.

The fresh palm stalk and planting action remain distinct from selected 213. The modern print places an unnumbered Chapter heading before this report; the selected digital grouping and historical print do not supply that separate heading.

segments.arabic: [216] حدثنا موسى بن إسماعيل قال: حدثنا همام أخبرنا إسحاق عن أنس بن مالك
segments.english: Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Hammam related to us. Ishaq informed us, from Anas ibn Malik:

segments.arabic: أن النبي ﷺ رأى أعرابيا يبول في المسجد، فقال دعوه حتى إذا فرغ دعا بماء فصبه عليه
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw a Bedouin urinating in the mosque and said: “Leave him.” When he had finished, he called for water and poured it over it.

notes: The instruction to leave the Bedouin, completion of the action and pouring water remain in order. The selected chain says informed us for Ishaq; the historical print says related to us. No instruction to strike or physically restrain anyone is inserted.

segments.arabic: [217] حدثنا أبو اليمان قال: أخبرنا شعيب عن الزهري قال: أخبرني عبيد الله بن عبد الله بن عتبة بن مسعود أن أبا هريرة قال
segments.english: Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: ‘Ubaydullah ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Utbah ibn Mas‘ud informed me that Abu Hurayrah said:

segments.arabic: قام أعرابي فبال في المسجد فتناوله الناس، فقال لهم النبي ﷺ دعوه وهريقوا على بوله سجلا من ماء أو ذنوبا من ماء فإنما بعثتم ميسرين ولم تبعثوا معسرين
segments.english: A Bedouin stood up and urinated in the mosque. The people confronted him, so the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to them: “Leave him, and pour a bucket of water—or a pail of water—over his urine. You have been sent to make things easy, and you have not been sent to make them difficult.”

notes: The full chain includes ibn Mas‘ud. The bucket-or-pail alternative remains. Confronted is used for the people’s response without inserting a physical strike or a quoted rebuke absent from this form. The repeated sent and not sent wording is retained.

segments.arabic: [219] حدثنا خالد قال وحدثنا سليمان عن يحيى بن سعيد قال: سمعت أنس بن مالك قال
segments.english: Khalid related to us. He said: And Sulayman related to us, from Yahya ibn Sa‘id, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik say:

segments.arabic: جاء أعرابي فبال في طائفة المسجد فزجره الناس فنهاهم النبي ﷺ فلما قضى بوله أمر النبي ﷺ بذنوب من ماء فأهريق عليه
segments.english: A Bedouin came and urinated in one part of the mosque. The people rebuked him, but the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, forbade them. When he had finished urinating, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, ordered a pail of water, which was poured over it.

notes: The selected short Khalid name, repeated reporting introduction and separate digital heading remain. The historical print supplies ibn Makhlad and joins this to the earlier chain with a transfer marker; those extra selected-source words are not supplied.

segments.arabic: [220] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن هشام بن عروة عن أبيه عن عائشة أم المؤمنين أنها قالت
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Hisham ibn ‘Urwah, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, the Mother of the Believers, who said:

segments.arabic: أتي رسول الله ﷺ بصبي فبال على ثوبه فدعا بماء فأتبعه إياه
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was brought a young boy, who urinated on his garment. He called for water and applied it to the urine.

notes: This and 221 occupy separate exact spans of the same original paragraph, retained in the source map. The Mother of the Believers designation is translated in full. Applying water to the urine renders the source’s following it with water; no rubbing procedure or extra wash is inserted.

segments.arabic: [221] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن ابن شهاب عن عبيد الله بن عبد الله بن عتبة عن أم قيس بنت محصن
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Ubaydullah ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Utbah, from Umm Qays bint Mihsan:

segments.arabic: أنها أتت بابن لها صغير لم يأكل الطعام إلى رسول الله ﷺ فأجلسه رسول الله ﷺ في حجره فبال على ثوبه فدعا بماء فنضحه ولم يغسله
segments.english: She brought a young son of hers who had not yet eaten food to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, seated him in his lap, and he urinated on his garment. He called for water and sprinkled it, without washing it.

notes: The third-person report, son not yet eating food, lap, garment, sprinkling and not washing remain. The English comparisons differ in describing the application of water; the working translation retains the distinct source verbs rather than merging sprinkling and washing. No feeding age or legal rule is added.

segments.arabic: [222] حدثنا آدم قال: حدثنا شعبة عن الأعمش عن أبي وائل عن حذيفة قال
segments.english: Adam related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from al-A‘mash, from Abu Wa’il, from Hudhayfah, who said:

segments.arabic: أتى النبي ﷺ سباطة قوم فبال قائما ثم دعا بماء فجئته بماء فتوضأ
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to a people’s refuse heap and urinated while standing. Then he called for water. I brought him water, and he performed ablution.

notes: Standing, the request for water, first-person response and ablution remain, with the full chain. No explanation of necessity or general permission is inserted.

segments.arabic: [223] حدثنا عثمان بن أبي شيبة قال: حدثنا جرير عن منصور عن أبي وائل عن حذيفة قال:
segments.english: ‘Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah related to us. He said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Abu Wa’il, from Hudhayfah, who said:

segments.arabic: رأيتني أنا والنبي ﷺ نتماشى فأتى سباطة قوم خلف حائط فقام كما يقوم أحدكم فبال فانتبذت منه فأشار إلي فجئته فقمت عند عقبه حتى فرغ
segments.english: I found myself walking with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He came to a people’s refuse heap behind a wall, stood as one of you stands, and urinated. I moved away from him, but he beckoned to me. I came to him and stood at his heel until he had finished.

notes: The shared walk, wall, standing comparison, moving away, beckoning and waiting remain. At his heel preserves the selected expression; no additional screening purpose from the chapter heading is inserted into the report.

segments.arabic: [224] حدثنا محمد بن عرعرة قال: حدثنا شعبة عن منصور عن أبي وائل قال:
segments.english: Muhammad ibn ‘Ar‘arah related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Mansur, from Abu Wa’il, who said:

segments.arabic: كان أبو موسى الأشعري يشدد في البول ويقول إن بني إسرائيل كان إذا أصاب ثوب أحدهم قرضه، فقال حذيفة ليته أمسك أتى رسول الله ﷺ سباطة قوم فبال قائما
segments.english: Abu Musa al-Ash‘ari used to be strict about urine. He would say: “Among the Children of Israel, when urine got onto someone’s garment, he would cut it out.” Hudhayfah said: “I wish he would refrain. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to a people’s refuse heap and urinated while standing.”

notes: The narrator’s account of Abu Musa and Hudhayfah’s response remain complete. The urine object follows the source context; no additional garment-cleaning procedure or legal commentary from the comparison footnote is included.
